moments.title: AI panic? History says this happened before
moments.insight: Rogers compares AI hysteria to past fears over railroads, electricity, and computers, calling it a recurring pattern, not something new.

moments.title: Why he painted his round-the-world car yellow
moments.insight: He chose yellow for his epic road trip specifically because its rarity made him visible, hoping it would protect him from danger.

moments.title: "I am lucky to be alive"
moments.insight: Reflecting on his multi-year drive through 116 countries, Rogers admits many who attempt such trips die, and he feels fortunate to have survived.

moments.title: What actually separates success from failure
moments.insight: Rogers argues that across all eras and countries, success simply comes down to ambitious people learning to work hard and do the right thing.

moments.title: The one piece of advice he repeats endlessly
moments.insight: He insists the single most important thing anyone can do is figure out what they truly love and pursue it, regardless of money or others' opinions.

moments.title: Why he waited until 60 to become a father
moments.insight: Rogers reveals he had his first child at 66 and second at 65, calling fatherhood the most exciting and best decision of his life.
